items.guidance: NetBox's Django project lives under netbox/, so a production Dockerfile would install pinned Python requirements, run python netbox/manage.py collectstatic --noinput, and start gunicorn on port 8000, optionally reusing contrib/gunicorn.py. Because NetBox normally relies on a reverse proxy for static files, serve them in-container, for example with WhiteNoise if added, and read ALLOWED_HOSTS, SECRET_KEY and database settings from environment variables in the configuration file.

contrib/gunicorn.py sets the loopback bind. Prefer overriding it at startup with gunicorn's --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 in the container CMD, or the GUNICORN_CMD_ARGS environment variable, rather than editing the contrib file.

Check whether NetBox already exposes an unauthenticated quick route, such as the API status endpoint under /api/; it may require login when LOGIN_REQUIRED is enabled or query the database. If no suitable route exists, add a minimal view in netbox/netbox/urls.py, and make sure it is exempt from NetBox's login-required middleware.

NetBox is a Django project, so a package.json migration script would not be expected. Confirm that python netbox/manage.py migrate --noinput works once a configuration.py reading DATABASE_* environment variables exists in the image.

Check whether NetBox runs its RQ jobs through the Django management command python netbox/manage.py rqworker, typically with the high, default and low queues. Report that command and whether it is a separate entry point that can be declared as a Procfile worker line. Also confirm that the Redis settings the worker reads, tasks and caching, can take the injected REDIS_URL.
